editorial.headline: Edible Ice and Dessert Ice With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers non-dairy edible ices, from sorbet to flavored ice premix, and the record treats it as nationally open and not moratorium-blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
This KBLI activity is about edible ice whose main ingredient is not milk. In practical terms, the record points to a broad family of frozen sweet products: sorbet, es lilin, ice drop, flavored ice variants, es mambo, es puter, and flavored ice premix. The emphasis is on food-grade frozen dessert ice, not the industrial or utility side of ice. That boundary is important because the record expressly leaves out dry ice, ice cubes, and block ice.

For founders, the commercial shape is therefore quite clear. This is the registration lane for businesses making edible frozen products where flavor, format, and consumer use define the activity. It can fit a very small producer as much as a scaled manufacturer, because the record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That matters: the code is not reserved only for large factories, and it is not limited to a cottage-scale interpretation. The same activity can sit across the full size range listed in the record.

The national foreign-investment picture is straightforward. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to full foreign ownership. There is no reduced foreign stake in the slim record, and no extra percentage to calculate. The only ownership number available is the national ceiling, so the responsible reading is simple: nationally, this is foreign-open up to 100%.

Bali does not add a separate foreign-ownership percentage here. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali reason says: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest Bali conclusion is not a warning dressed up as nuance: on this record, a foreign-owned registration is nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
